meta.what: PATCH SPECIFICATION ONLY. No source file was edited. Every record says which constant to change, where it lives, what it is now, what the manufacturer CAD says it should be, and what that is expected to do. Three airframes are being corrected against the same two source files, so the edits are applied in one later pass.
meta.why_this_airframe: mini2 is the Das comparison airframe that ALREADY agrees best (|dL| 0.51 dB). The first job here is not to improve it, it is not to break it. Every record below therefore carries an explicit 'do not touch' counterpart list, and nothing is changed that the CAD does not force.
meta.blind_rule: NO sigma quantity was read or computed while writing this file. outputs/das_fleet_*.json, p3_*.json, phantom3/* and rcs_anchor.json were not opened. expected_sigma_direction below is a PREDICTION written in advance precisely so it can be falsified later.

evidence_base.cad: DJI's own published GLB of the WM161 (DJI Mini 2), unfolded: /tmp scratch copy of WM161_zhankai_1k.glb, 7,707,032 bytes, 59 parts, 109,470 faces, native units metres. Provenance and URL in assets/photos/mini2/SOURCES.md section 4; spec provenance in outputs/mini2_specs.json.
evidence_base.photos: assets/photos/mini2/ (86 files + SOURCES.md). Used this round ONLY as corroboration, never as the source of a number - see n_from_photo.
evidence_base.published: DJI Mini 2 User Manual v1.0 (2020.11) pp.45-47, international version.

meta.measurement_method: EDGE-BASED (1D). Every truth value below is a distance between two identified features - hub centre to hub centre, arm underside to foot, bell top to screw-head top, motor axis to fairing tip along the arm axis - taken on named GLB parts with the scene-graph world transform applied. Whole-mesh bounding boxes are used only for the scale check, never to set a constant.

frame_convention.axes: glTF (+y up, +z nose) -> repo (X = +nose, Y = +left, Z = +up): X = z_glb, Y = x_glb, Z = y_glb, scaled to mm.
frame_convention.origin_x: fore-aft centre of the fuselage shell, GLB part 'Default_4'. This is the repo's existing choice (build_frame_cad always builds the shell at the origin) and is kept.
frame_convention.origin_z: the aircraft's lowest non-propeller point is defined as z = -24.52 mm, which reproduces the repo's existing published-height decomposition exactly (-24.52 .. +31.46 = 55.98 = the published 56 mm). All z values below are in that frame.
frame_convention.rotor_order: index 0,1,2,3 = rotor_deg (63.14, 133.70, 226.30, 296.86) = front-left, rear-left, rear-right, front-right.

meta.rel_err_pct_definition: signed relative error of the CURRENT (old) modelled quantity against the CAD truth, (old - truth) / truth * 100. It is the error the record removes, not the size of the edit.

scale_check.verdict: PASS - the GLB is used at native metre scale with NO scale factor applied.

checks.quantity: props-excluded bounding box L x W x H
checks.how: all 59 parts except the 8 propeller-blade meshes (polySurface95/89/81/61/102/84/80/58)
centre of front-left motor bell (polySurface76) to centre of rear-right bell (polySurface90); the two diagonals agree to 0.00 mm
GLB part 'Default_4' alone, against the published FOLDED length, which the fuselage sets

max vertex radius about each bell centre, front pair then rear pair. DJI publishes no propeller geometry (manual, QSG and the standalone Propellers User Guide all checked) so this one has no published comparand.

scale_check.conclusion: Two independent DJI artefacts - the CAD and the specification table - agree to <= 0.25 % on every quantity that both of them carry. The CAD is therefore treated as the dimensional truth for shape constants, and the published table stays the truth for the forced envelope.

envelope_forcing.why_this_is_the_priority: frame_fit_scale multiplies the finished frame by sz to make its bounding box equal the published height. sz != 1 means the shape is being falsified to pay for a modelling error somewhere else. On phantom3 this was driven from 4.4 % to 0.2 %; here it is currently 9.4 %.

now.what_it_costs: the measured 46.16 mm fuselage shell is squashed to 41.8 mm (-9.4 %), and every other vertical dimension with it. The error being absorbed is NOT in the shell - it is in the arms, the legs and a missing part.

cause_1.what: landing foot is 10.65 mm too LOW
cause_1.why: rotor_z_mm currently moves the propellers only; build_frame_cad builds all four arms, all four motors and the two landing posts on ONE z plane (0.012*diag), so the front arm - which the CAD puts 21.44 mm above the rear one - sits at the mean instead.

cause_2.what: top of the aircraft is 4.81 mm too LOW
cause_2.why: the modelled top is the fuselage crown. The real top is the pair of propeller-mount screw heads standing above each motor bell, which are not modelled at all.

residual_decomposition.note: 10.65 - 4.81 = 5.84 = the excess, to the last recorded digit. The decomposition closes with no remainder, which is why both causes are treated as real and neither is absorbed into a fudge.

arithmetic.from: MOTOR_BASE_Z 7.985 + 10.63 (front rotor dz) + motor_h 7.1 + screw-head stand 5.47
arithmetic.residual_source: rotor_z_mm is +-10.63 (measured from the two propeller mid-planes) while the two motor-bell bases are +-10.905 apart and the two arm axes +-10.72. Keeping the propeller-derived 10.63 leaves 0.275 mm on the bell height. Changing rotor_z_mm to chase it would move the propellers, which are already right, so it is left as a declared residual.

envelope_forcing.warning_partial_application_is_worse_tha: F1+F4 alone (arms/gear follow rotor_z_mm, no screw heads) gives a raw height of 51.19 mm and sz = 1.094 - the same 9.4 % distortion with the sign flipped. F1, F3, F4 and F6 must land together or not at all.
envelope_forcing.sx_sy: unchanged at 1.0 - envelope_mm is (None, None, 56.0) and STAYS height-only (house rule, same as mini5pro / mavic4pro / matrice4e / typhoonh480 / phantom3 / m350rtk). The width record F5 therefore does NOT act through the fit scale; it corrects the mesh directly.

fixes.constant: _arm_folding z0/z1 for the mini2 arms - the arm plane must follow rotor_z_mm
fixes.old: z0 = 0.0, z1 = 0.012*diag = 2.556 mm for all four arms
fixes.new: z0 = dz_k, z1 = 0.012*diag + dz_k, with dz_k = spec.rotor_z_mm[k]/1000 -> front arms +10.63 mm, rear arms -10.63 mm. Gate it on a new per-key opt-in (e.g. ARM_Z_FOLLOWS_ROTOR = {'mini2': True}) so every other airframe stays bit-identical.
fixes.evidence: Arm axis measured by cutting the arm assembly PERPENDICULAR to its own axis at r = 70..100 mm. Front (polySurface201): axis z = +13.64 / +13.68 / +13.91 at r 70-80 / 80-90 / 90-100, section height 14.15 mm, underside +6.56..+6.81. Rear (polySurface101): axis z = -7.43 / -7.76 / -8.19 over the same bands, underside -14.24..-14.64. Half-separation of the two arm axes = 10.72 mm; the registry already carries rotor_z_mm = +-10.63 (measured independently from the two propeller mid-planes, 21.25 mm apart). The two independent measurements of the same physical offset agree to 0.09 mm. Mean of the two arm axes = +2.96 mm against the engine's 0.012*diag = 2.556 mm, i.e. the CURRENT single plane is the correct mean - the defect is that there is only one plane.
fixes.rel_err_note: front arm axis modelled at 2.556 against a true 13.68 mm; expressed against the 21.44 mm true front-to-rear separation the model has 0 % of it.
fixes.expected_sigma_direction: PREDICTION: azimuth-mean sigma up slightly (order +0.2 to +0.5 dB) at low elevation, because removing the sz=0.906 squash restores 9.4 % of vertical projected area to the fuselage and arms; near zero change at nadir/zenith where the projection is horizontal. Separately, the front and rear rotor stations become genuinely 21.3 mm apart in z, so the front/rear two-scatterer interference pattern at non-zero elevation will move - lobe positions change even where the mean does not.
fixes.risk: SHARED CODE. mini5pro also carries rotor_z_mm = (-12, +2, +2, -12); if this is applied unconditionally its mesh changes and any mini5pro result already on disk is invalidated. Must be key-gated. Second, the rear arm really slopes DOWN going outboard (-5.89 at r 60-70 to -8.19 at r 90-100) while a uniform dz keeps the engine's upward tip rise - a 2.5 mm slope-sign error over 40 mm that this record does not fix and that should be declared, not hidden.

fixes.constant: MOTOR_BASE_Z['mini2']  (motor bell base z, mean plane)
fixes.evidence: Mean of the two measured bell bases: (18.89 + (-2.92)) / 2 = 7.985 mm. With F2's dz this puts the front bell base at 18.615 (CAD 18.89) and the rear at -2.645 (CAD -2.92). The engine's default 0.014*diag = 2.982 mm sits essentially ON the arm axis, i.e. it buries the bell to half its height inside the arm; the CAD puts the bell base 5.21 mm (front) / 4.84 mm (rear) ABOVE the arm axis, sitting on top of the arm end as a motor physically does. The proportional rule is what fails here: the Mini 2's arm section (14.15 mm) is unusually large against its 213 mm diagonal.

fixes.evidence: Radial profile of each arm assembly along its OWN axis. Front (polySurface201, axis 63.14 deg, hub r 98.43): structure continues to s = 113.52 mm, i.e. 15.09 mm past the motor axis, with transverse width tapering 19.4 -> 13.4 -> 10.6 -> 7.0 mm over s 98..114 and z from +8.6 to +19.1. The widest vertex of the entire aircraft is (50.34, 101.72, 13.11) at s = 113.49 - it is this fairing, not the motor bell, that carries the published 203 mm width. Rear (polySurface101, axis 133.69 deg, hub r 116.92): structure continues to s = 126.22, i.e. 9.30 mm past the motor axis, and it is this fairing that sets the aircraft's rearmost point at X = -90.28 mm. fixes.rel_err_note: modelled frame width 193.821 mm against the CAD's 203.43 mm.
fixes.expected_sigma_direction: PREDICTION: sigma UP at the azimuths where a front arm tip is broadside (roughly +-60 deg from the nose), order +0.1 to +0.4 dB, because ~2 x (14 x 10 x 15 mm) of moulded plastic appears where there was nothing. Plastic group |Gamma| ~ 0.28, so the effect is modest. Near-nose and near-tail aspects: ~0.
fixes.risk: TWO risks, both declared. (a) ARM_TIP_OVERHANG is currently a per-key SCALAR; the Mini 2 needs different values front and rear, so the engine must accept a per-rotor tuple. That is the same generalisation already made for r_motor in _gear_motor_legs (src/drone_cad.py:1422-1423), and a scalar entry must keep behaving exactly as today. If the tuple is refused, use the front value 0.01509 for all four and accept that the rearmost point overshoots to about X = -96 mm (+3.6 % on length) - which would be WORSE than doing nothing, so in that case skip the record. (b) _arm_folding sweeps a constant 2*arm_r1 = 9.0 mm wide tip section, while the real fairing has tapered to 6.96 mm by s = 113.5. The measured 15.09 mm overhang therefore lands the mesh's max |Y| at about 103.3 mm against a true 101.72 - the width error goes from -4.7 % to +1.6 %, not to zero. An overhang of 13.33 mm would hit 101.72 exactly, and it is REJECTED here: that number is solved from the envelope, not measured on the part, and this repository's whole claim rests on shape constants being measurements. The +1.6 % is recorded as a residual to be removed later by tapering the tip section, not by bending the overhang.

CORROBORATED BY PHOTOGRAPH, not measured from it: assets/photos/mini2/mini2_t28_fcc_mt2wd_propeller_motor_view.jpg (FCC exhibit, ruler in frame) shows the mounted propeller held by exactly two cross-head screws, diametrically opposite, one at each end of the prop hub, standing proud of the hub face - and shows they are STEEL, which is why the group is 'motor' (metal) and not the plastic body group.
fixes.rel_err_note: modelled top +26.647 mm (the fuselage crown) against a true +31.46 mm.
fixes.expected_sigma_direction: PREDICTION: negligible in its own right, |dsigma| < 0.1 dB. At the Das band (21-27 GHz, lambda 11-14 mm) a 3.8 mm square post is roughly 0.3 lambda - a Rayleigh-regime scatterer, and there are only eight of them. Its whole value is that it removes the need for a 9.4 % vertical squash. If a later round finds these eight posts moving sigma by more than a few tenths of a dB, that is evidence the model is over-sensitive to sub-wavelength detail and should be reported as such.
fixes.risk: The CAD shows the screw heads FLOATING 4.6 mm above the bell top, because the propeller hub that fills the gap belongs to the blade meshes. Building them as floating boxes would add an interior surface with no support, so the spec builds a solid post from the bell top to the measured head top. That post's shank is 4.6 mm of geometry the CAD does not draw - declared. Second, azimuth: the screws rotate with the motor, so their absolute azimuth in the CAD is an arbitrary frozen pose. Aligning them with the arm axis (ang, ang+180) is a JUDGED choice; at r = 5.0 mm they stay well inside the 9.1 mm bell radius so it cannot change any silhouette.

do_not_touch.why: height-only forcing is the house rule shared with mini5pro/mavic4pro/matrice4e/typhoonh480/phantom3/m350rtk. After the patch the free length and width land within 0.6 % and 1.6 % of the CAD, which will look like an invitation to force them too. Forcing L/W converts frame_fit_scale into an anisotropic squash and manufactures a 0 % agreement that is a constraint, not evidence.
the modelled motor-to-motor diagonal already reproduces the CAD's 213.05 mm to +0.02 %. Nothing in this round touches the planform.

these are the PUBLISHED envelope, VERIFIED grade, used as the denominators of the shell ratios. Replacing them with the CAD's 159.11 / 203.43 / 55.98 would silently rescale every shell ratio for a 0.2 % gain and would demote a manufacturer-published number to a measured one.

do_not_touch.item: _SHELL_SHAPE['mini2'] fl / fw / fh / npow / hw / hh / zo
do_not_touch.why: the built shell's bounding box is 48.36 mm tall against the CAD's 46.16 (+4.8 %), and the temptation is to shave fh to absorb it. Do not. The 22 station numbers ARE the measurement; the +4.8 % is spline overshoot in the loft, an engine artefact. Retuning fh would corrupt a measurement to patch the engine. After F1/F3/F6 the shell no longer sets the bounding box at all, so this residual stops touching the fit scale.

F5 moves the arm TIP outboard to s = 113.5 mm where the real fairing has narrowed to 6.96 mm, which argues for arm_r1 = 3.48. Resist it: arm_r1 also feeds z_arm = 0.012*diag - arm_r1*h_ratio/2, and at 4.5 that expression lands the landing-post attachment at +6.549 mm against a CAD-measured arm underside of +6.56..+6.81. methodology_guard.rule: shape constants come from CAD, photographs and published specification. They are never chosen to move sigma, and no sigma file was opened while this specification was written.
methodology_guard.why_it_matters_here: in the phantom3 round the silhouette IoU improved while the sigma proxy went the other way, and that disagreement is the evidence that the meshes are not being tuned toward the published RCS. A record that improved both would be weaker, not stronger. The predictions in expected_sigma_direction are written down now so that a later sigma run can falsify them.
